title: How has mathematics moved humanity forward?
description: Patterns in the Moon and planets, and patterns in living things, became rules that carried people to space and helped doctors cure disease. The video ends on the open discussion the book asks for.
teaching_notes: One idea: patterns that are understood become rules, and rules have moved people forward in science, medicine and building. Any honest example from the child is welcome. Watch for students who think mathematics stays inside the classroom.

source: Figure it Out Q2 (Math Talk), p.2
video_script.why: The child sees that patterns, once explained, became rules that launched satellites and helped doctors, so mathematics moves people forward.
video_script.substitution: Patterns that are understood become rules, and rules carry people forward.
video_script.anchor: the Moon and planets, a rocket and a satellite, and a doctor with a medical chart, the three ways forward
video_script.payoff_line: Patterns that are understood become rules that carry us forward

final_answer.value: the theory of gravitation; satellites and rockets; finding and curing diseases
final_answer.spoken: the theory of gravitation, satellites and rockets, and the finding and curing of diseases

hold_back: Patterns that are understood become rules that carry us forward
maths_rules: space: patterns in the motion of the Moon and planets led to the theory of gravitation
technology: that theory lets us launch satellites and send rockets to the Moon and Mars
medicine: patterns in the genes of living things help doctors find and cure diseases
open discussion: any honest example, such as building bridges, running an economy or making machines, is acceptable
video_script.design: One idea: understood patterns become rules that move people forward. Callback to the earlier video on why mathematics asks why. Wrong idea: none is broken. The three examples stay on the board to the end.
